title: The Housing Authority sold 440 Turk for $4.9 million without an asset register entry

beats.text: San Francisco authorized buying 440 Turk Street from its Housing Authority.

visual.sub: The City approved a purchase ceiling and required an appraisal

beats.text: The price could not exceed $5 million or the approved appraised value.
The Housing Authority’s audit records a $4.9 million sale in September 2018.
Its capital asset register had no corresponding entry for the building.

visual.kicker: The Housing Authority sold the building for $4.9 million without a corresponding asset entry

beats.text: The auditor did not say the sale proceeds disappeared.

visual.kicker: The Housing Authority sold the building for $4.9 million without a corresponding asset entry

beats.text: The same audit found a different problem with a Hunters View property.

visual.kicker: A Hunters View disposal was recorded in the wrong year

beats.text: Its disposal was recorded in a later year.

visual.kicker: A Hunters View disposal was recorded in the wrong year

beats.text: Auditors recommended comparing a detailed inventory with the general ledger.

visual.kicker: The FY2019 audit recorded the capital asset finding as corrected

beats.text: The following audit marked finding 2018-004 corrected.

visual.kicker: The FY2019 audit recorded the capital asset finding as corrected

beats.text: The closing statement would establish the full disposition of the proceeds.
